standard.title: Use suitable materials and techniques
standard.description: Select and use suitable materials, components, tools, equipment and techniques to safely make designed solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can select and use materials, components, tools, equipment and techniques to safely make designed solutions (AC9TDE4P03). They have selected and used tools and materials with guidance. They have not yet matched selection decisions to design intention with explicit justification, or applied the full range of safety, hygiene and environmental considerations across material types.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students select materials, components, tools, equipment and techniques that match the design intention and use them safely — applying appropriate safety, hygiene and environmental practices for the context.

nodes.label: Matching materials and techniques to the design intention
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select materials and techniques that match the design intention and explain why each choice is appropriate
nodes.minimum_width: Select a material and technique for a specific task and explain why each matches the design intention — referencing at least one material property
nodes.typical_width: Choose appropriate materials, tools, equipment and techniques for a specific design purpose; explain how the selection matches the design intention — considering function, aesthetics and sustainability; demonstrate that the selection produces the intended result
wider: Match material and joining techniques to the design intention for a textile project (e.g. a community banner, a fabric bag) — accurately cutting and joining fabric pieces as specified by the design
Select and sequence materials, tools and equipment for an electronic product — explaining how each component choice supports the circuit's intended function
Select and justify materials for a water-resistant, floating craft — explaining which material properties (density, water resistance, structural strength) determine the selection

response_modes.reason: Students typically select familiar materials by habit rather than matching properties to design intention. Multiple production contexts — textiles, electronics, food, structural — each requiring different property reasoning help students build the habit of justifying selection against design requirements rather than defaulting to familiarity.

success_criteria: Selects materials and techniques appropriate for the design intention
Explains the selection by referencing at least one relevant material property or technique characteristic
nodes.hinge_reason: Material and technique selection in N1 determines what safety practices apply in N2 — students who cannot match materials to design intention will select inappropriate tools or techniques, making N2's safety and hygiene requirements impossible to apply correctly.

nodes.label: Working safely and applying food, hygiene and environmental practices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and apply the relevant safety, hygiene and environmental practices for their production context
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two relevant safety or hygiene practices for a specific production task and apply them correctly
nodes.typical_width: Apply appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), safe work practices, hygiene standards and environmental considerations relevant to the production context — whether food preparation, garden cultivation or construction of electronic or structural products; explain why each practice is required
wider: Apply food safety and hygiene practices in preparing a food product — including washing produce to remove residues, safe disposal of cooking oils, refrigerated storage of perishables, and managing food allergen risks
Apply safe work practices for construction tasks (e.g. protective eyewear, safe tool handling) — explaining how each practice prevents a specific risk
Identify environmental considerations when making with materials — e.g. safe disposal of chemical residues, minimising material waste, selecting materials with lower environmental impact

response_modes.reason: Safety and hygiene practices require consistent application across contexts, not just recognition. Students who can name practices but don't apply them consistently need deliberate practice opportunities where the habit is formed through repetition across different production contexts.

success_criteria: Applies at least two relevant safety or hygiene practices correctly for the production context
Can explain why each practice is required
